title: 2011 AMC 10B Problem 13
statement: Two real numbers are selected independently at random from the interval \([-20, 10].\) What is the probability that the product of those numbers is greater than zero?

solutions.text:
A selected number is negative with probability \(\frac{20}{30}=\frac{2}{3}\) and positive with probability \(\frac{10}{30}=\frac{1}{3}.\) (Selecting exactly \(0\) has probability \(0.\)) The product is positive exactly when both numbers have the same sign, so the probability is \[\left(\dfrac23\right)^2+\left(\dfrac13\right)^2=\dfrac49+\dfrac19=\dfrac59.\]

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: The product is positive when both numbers have the same sign
The interval has \(20\) negative units and \(10\) positive units
